edge.title: SODA anchor pull of hidden matrices toward init, cosine-faded
edge.summary: Adds a SODA-style anchor to every Muon hidden matrix: before each update the weights are mixed toward their initial value, p ← (1−λ)p + λ·p_init with λ = fade(t)/(t+2). Unrolled, this keeps only a (s+2)/(t+2)-weighted sum of past updates as the displacement from init (dual averaging with linearly growing weights), so early updates are progressively forgotten; for the zero-initialized proj matrices it is pure shrinkage toward 0. The pull runs at full strength until step 2000 and is cosine-faded to 0 by 2750 so the final approach is plain #20 Muon; everything else is #20 and the claim moves 3030→3000.

changes.label: Anchor pull toward initial weights
changes.detail: On a param's first Muon step state['soda_anchor'] = p.clone() (the init); every step, after the update and u/w-floor scale are computed from the current p, p.mul_(1−λ).add_(anchor, alpha=λ) runs before p.add_(update, −lr).

changes.label: λ = fade(t)/(t+2), cosine fade
changes.detail: lam = clamp(SODA_LAMBDA_SCALE·soda_fade_multiplier(step_count)/(step_count+2), 0, 1): 1/(t+2) up to step 2000 (≈5e-4 there), then 0.5(1+cos(πx)) over steps 2000–2750, 0 afterwards.

changes.label: Data glob + logging
changes.detail: Train/val shards found via Path(pattern).parent.glob(name) (same files and order), import math, SODA settings logged.

edge.parent_check: consistent (diff vs #20 only adds the SODA anchor plus a cosmetic data-glob change; train_steps 3040 / PowerCool end 3105 unchanged)

hparams.hidden.optimizer: Muon + SOAP (MLP, V) + Contra→Soft-Muon + NorMuon-lite + SODA anchor

mechanisms.name: SODA-style anchor toward init
mechanisms.explain: Each hidden matrix stores its value at its first Muon step (the initialization) as an anchor; on every step, before the Muon update is applied, the weights are mixed p ← (1−λ)p + λ·anchor with λ = fade(t)/(t+2). With d_t = p_t − p_init and fade = 1 this gives d_{t+1} = −Σ_s ((s+2)/(t+2))·η_s·u_s, i.e. dual averaging with linearly increasing weights and a growing proximal pull, so old updates decay; for zero-initialized proj matrices the anchor is 0 and it acts as a 1/(t+2) decoupled weight decay. fade = 1 until step 2000, then cosine to 0 at 2750, after which training is plain Muon.

caveats: README frames the idea as optimistic dual averaging, but the only code change is the anchor mixing; no extra optimistic/extrapolated-gradient term is added (Muon's existing Nesterov-style momentum is unchanged). The u/w-floor scale is computed from p before the anchor pull is applied. Runs were made on 4×H200 (torchrun nproc_per_node=4, gradient accumulation keeps the global batch), n=9.
